requirement:
TBV automatically redacts recognized credentials in source excerpts delivered
by its inspection tools and in node text supplied to its agent requests.
The built-in rules replace recognized secret regions with redaction markers
while preserving line breaks. SDK-supplied outline languages use the same redacted
regions, so changing only a recognized credential does not change its
structural fingerprint.

Loaded source snapshots retain the original text for selection and spans;
redaction applies when preparing model-visible text and structural hashes.
Filesystem evidence storage preserves the supplied record. Applications supply
their own answer values and remain responsible for what those answers contain.
Habeas additionally recognizes explicit credentials in its configuration files
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.sources.redaction`, and each assertion enforces the stated outcome.

**Inspection-tool excerpts.** The dispatch code in `project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_,%20D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[dispatch]` is the `{impl}` site. It delivers source text through `read_source`, `search_text`, `search_structure` and `get_source_page`.
- `fixed_source_reads_redact_delivery_and_propagate_preparation_errors` checks `read_source`. The returned text has no raw token, contains `[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`, and keeps the same line count as the raw text. The dependency fingerprint is computed from the raw content. A preparation error propagates.
- `search_excerpts_redact_credentials_before_serialization_and_paging` checks `search_text` and, when the `default-languages` feature is on, `search_structure`. It uses a GitHub token and a multi-line RSA private key. It reassembles the paged output and asserts the exact expected excerpt, equal line counts, and that neither the token nor any key-body line appears. It also checks that the file on disk is unchanged.

**Node text in agent requests.** `queued_contents_and_graph_read_tools_redact_credentials_before_delivery` runs `contents_of_current_node` and the `read_node` tool. It asserts that no request's chat history, which includes the initial prompt, contains the raw token and that every request contains the marker. The mandatory input showed the `secret` literal as the marker only because the tool display redacted it; the habeas tool output notes this. The dependency fingerprint and the graph contents still hold the original text.

**Marker replacement and line breaks.** The redaction unit tests cover these points.
- `private_keys_are_redacted_from_header_through_body_keeping_lines`: a private key is replaced from header through body with line counts preserved.
- `tokens_in_code_are_redacted_without_adjacent_code`: adjacent code is left intact.
- `regions_extend_both_ways_keep_crlf_and_scan_past_a_mebibyte`: CRLF line endings are kept, and the scan works on input past one mebibyte.
- `slices_concatenate_to_the_redacted_whole`: slices join to the redacted whole.
- `heuristic_findings_alone_are_not_redacted`: only recognized credentials are redacted.
- `configuration_keys_do_not_add_sdk_specific_secret_rules`: configuration keys such as `api_key` add no SDK-specific rules.

**Same regions for SDK outline languages, and structural fingerprints.**
- `hashes_do_not_depend_on_credential_values` shows that changing only a token leaves structural hashes equal for Rust and text. It also shows that changing code outside a redacted region still changes the hash.
- `redaction_never_changes_an_outline` checks that redaction does not change the outline for YAML, Rust, TOML, Markdown and text. It also checks that line counts are preserved.
- `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` shows that a changed credential leaves the fingerprint unchanged, which is the structural-fingerprint obligation.

**Original text retained.** In the same `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` test, `text()` equals the source, and a selected node's `text()` still holds the token while its `format()` does not.

**Storage and application answers.** `storage_preserves_completed_answers_containing_credential_shaped_text` stores and loads an answer containing a token. It asserts that the loaded output equals the original and that the file bytes contain the token.

The Habeas configuration-file credentials clause is only a `{cite}` of `requirements.authoring.credentials`. It needs no test here.

I found no untested obligation and no assertion that contradicts the requirement.

text: :::{req} redaction
TBV automatically redacts recognized credentials in source excerpts delivered
by its inspection tools and in node text supplied to its agent requests.
The built-in rules replace recognized secret regions with redaction markers
while preserving line breaks. SDK-supplied outline languages use the same redacted
regions, so changing only a recognized credential does not change its
structural fingerprint.
Loaded source snapshots retain the original text for selection and spans;
redaction applies when preparing model-visible text and structural hashes.
Filesystem evidence storage preserves the supplied record. Applications supply
their own answer values and remain responsible for what those answers contain.
Habeas additionally recognizes explicit credentials in its configuration files
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`.
:::{req} credentials
Bedrock configurations MAY supply `credentials` containing nonempty
`access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, and optional nonempty `session_token`.
Ollama and OpenAI configurations MAY supply a nonempty `api_key`. Habeas MUST reject a
Bedrock record combining explicit credentials with `aws_profile`, and an Ollama or OpenAI
record combining `api_key` with `api_key_env`.
Explicit credentials MUST be passed directly to the selected provider without
changing process environment variables or writing credential files. Saved
explicit values MUST round-trip; credentials resolved from profiles or the
environment MUST NOT be serialized back. Debug output, configuration diagnostics,
usage records, and initial prompts MUST NOT include credential values. TOML
diagnostics MUST NOT echo credential-containing source lines. A configuration
file containing explicit credentials MAY be read as source; its credential
values MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`.
Validation MUST report a workspace `habeas.toml` present in the Git index that
contains explicit credentials, naming the file and the credential fields and
recommending credential-source references, because committed credentials leak.
Documentation MUST discourage literal credentials in workspace files and
recommend AWS profiles or environment-variable references. Examples MUST use
placeholders and explain that workspace files may be committed or read as source
when explicitly allowed.
